pl-l2d26c4-d1e108.summary: States that good will itself precedes some gifts of grace.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e111.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: good will precedes many of God's gifts, but not all; in those it does not precede it is present and helps; mercy both prevents and follows (Ps 58:11; 22:6), preventing the unwilling and following the willing; we pray for enemies that God may work in them to will, and ask that he who made us will may give what we will.
claims: Good will precedes many but not all of God's gifts.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e114.summary: Concludes that good will precedes some gifts, being accompanied by helping grace, and is preceded by others, namely operating grace, faith with charity.
claims: Good will precedes cooperating grace and is preceded by operating grace.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e118.summary: Notes that Augustine elsewhere seems to make faith come from will: on 'with the heart one believes unto justice,' a man can enter a church or approach the altar unwilling but cannot believe unwilling.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e121.summary: Adds the gloss on Genesis, where Laban and Bethuel ask Rebecca's will: faith is of will, not necessity.
claims: Faith is of will, not necessity.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e124.summary: Replies that these texts do not mean faith comes from man's will, since faith is properly God's gift and good merits begin from it; by faith the impious is justified and faith then works through love. Rather, there is faith only in one who wills to believe, whose good will faith precedes not in time but in cause and nature.
claims: Faith is God's gift and the beginning of merit.
Faith precedes good will in cause and nature, not in time.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e129.summary: Explains Augustine's saying that good will is in and helps the gifts it does not precede: it helps them by consenting toward good, and is in them because they do not precede it in time.
claims: Good will is simultaneous with the gifts that cause it.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e132.summary: Raises a sharper difficulty from De praedestinatione sanctorum on 'not that we are sufficient to think anything of ourselves': thinking comes before believing, since no one believes without first thinking it should be believed; if good thought is not from us, neither is belief, believing being thinking with assent. This seems to make good thought, and so good will, precede faith.

pl-l2d26c4-d1e135.summary: Replies that some good thought or will sometimes precedes faith, but not the good will by which one lives rightly, which is not without faith and charity. Augustine to Anastasius: without the Spirit the will is not free, being conquered by desires; it is freed only when charity is poured into hearts and grace frees it by the law of faith, that is, faith working through love; fruit not rising from charity's root is not good.
claims: The good will of right living requires faith and charity.
The will is freed only by the Spirit and faith working through love.

pl-l2d26c4.summary: Notes that good will itself precedes some gifts of grace: Augustine says good will precedes many of God's gifts but not all, and is present in and helps those it does not precede; mercy prevents and follows. So good will precedes gifts of cooperating grace and is preceded by operating grace, faith with charity. Augustine elsewhere seems to make faith come from the will (one can enter a church unwilling but not believe unwilling; faith is of will, not necessity), but this means faith exists only in one who wills to believe, and faith precedes that good will in cause and nature, not in time. A harder objection: Augustine says thinking comes before believing and good thinking is not from us, suggesting good thought and will precede faith. Lombard answers that some good thought or will precedes faith, but not the good will by which one lives rightly, which does not exist without faith and charity, since the will is free for good only when freed by the Spirit and faith working through love.
claims: Good will precedes some gifts of grace and is preceded by others.
Good will is preceded by operating grace, faith with charity.
Faith is said to be of the will because it exists only in one who wills to believe.
Faith precedes good will in cause and nature, not in time.
Some good thought precedes faith, but not the good will of right living.
The will is free for good only when freed by the Spirit and faith working through love.
